identifier_concepts.MAEASaM ID: The human-readable business-key identifier (e.g. RS-SEN-00000001) manually entered by data recorders. This is the field present in every Metadata Template, described as 'Primary Key' in Operational Info — but that label is at the conceptual/business level, not Arches' actual storage mechanism (see resourceinstanceid below).
identifier_concepts.Arches resourceinstanceid: The UUID Arches assigns automatically to every resource instance in every model (e.g. b42c81bf-1493-417d-993d-24862c11d545). It is not a node in any graph and does not need a template field — it's an intrinsic, system-level attribute of the resource record, confirmed present in real exports (Datasets/*.csv 'uuid' column) and used internally for map layers and Resource-Instance-List relationships. Foreign Key references between resources are actually stored via this UUID, not the MAEASaM ID string.
identifier_concepts.ARK Identifier: STATUS: under consideration, not yet implemented. A globally resolvable, citable persistent identifier (Archival Resource Key scheme) the project is considering for long-term external citation of resources — distinct from both MAEASaM ID and resourceinstanceid above. Needs a NAAN registration decision, a target field/node, and a minting workflow before it can be added to any template. See Task_List.md.

input_instructions.Concept-list: Please write the term exactly as recorded in the "{collection}" controlled vocabulary.
input_instructions.String: Please enter the information as free text.
input_instructions.Resource-Instance-List: Please write the MAEASaM ID of the relevant record from the "{collection}" resource instance.
input_instructions.Date: Please enter the date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD).
input_instructions.EDTF: Please enter the date using the Extended Date/Time Format (EDTF) standard. See the EDTF specification for guidance: https://www.loc.gov/standards/datetime/ Note: avoid the combined uncertain+approximate qualifier (%) - a known Arches issue currently drops it on save (see known_issues below). The single '?' (uncertain) and '~' (approximate) qualifiers work correctly.
input_instructions.Boolean: Please enter either "Yes" or "No" as the value.
input_instructions.Auto-Populated: This field is automatically populated by the system. Leave this field blank.
input_instructions.Derived: This field is automatically derived from the linked resource record(s). Leave this field blank.
input_instructions.GeoJSON-feature-collection: Please provide the geometry as coordinates in Well-Known Text (WKT) format.
input_instructions.Number: Please enter a numeric value only (no units or additional text).
input_instructions.URL: Please enter a complete, valid web address (URL), including the http:// or https:// prefix.

input_instructions_csv._comment: Shorter, cell-ready versions of the entries above, used when the full input_instructions text reads as too long/verbose inside an actual spreadsheet cell. Only entries that intentionally diverge from input_instructions are listed here; anything not listed uses the full text as-is.
input_instructions_csv.EDTF: Please enter the date using the Extended Date/Time Format (EDTF) standard (https://www.loc.gov/standards/datetime/). Avoid the combined '%' qualifier - a known Arches issue drops it on save; '?' and '~' alone work fine.

necessity_definitions.Mandatory: Mandatory to add a value in this field.
necessity_definitions.Strongly recommended: Not mandatory but good to use to provide context.
necessity_definitions.Mandatory if (x): Mandatory only when the condition specified in x is met. For example, for the metadata field "Digitised Date", Mandatory if (Is Digitised) means that this field must be completed when "Is Digitised" is true. If "Is Digitised" is false, the field is considered Optional.
necessity_definitions.Mandatory if applicable: Mandatory only when the field is relevant to this particular resource; otherwise it does not need a value.
necessity_definitions.If applicable: Fill in only when the information exists or applies to this resource; otherwise leave blank.

operational_info_definitions.Primary Key: Key value of the table, MAEASaM ID. Each table has only one.
operational_info_definitions.Foreign Key: Key value of another related table (resource instance) represented in this table.
operational_info_definitions.Derived: Values which can be created by deriving from a related table (resource instance).
operational_info_definitions.Auto-Populated: Automatically created values by the database, such as uploader or upload/modified date.
operational_info_definitions.N/A: A regular, directly-entered field that is not a key, not derived from another table, and not auto-populated by the system.

spreadsheet_formatting_rules: Use 12 point font size for all characters.
Use Calibri font for all characters.
Use bold only for the row labels in the first 3 columns (Arches terminology / Universal terminology / User form). The rest of the page should be written in normal (non-bold) weight.

Do not use wrap text: turn wrap text off for all cells, so every row stays one line high and the sheet stays compact (changed 2026-09-24 from the earlier "Use wrap text for all cells." rule, by the user's decision).
Use All Borders for every cell.

Colour-code each field's Metadata (En/Fr/Ar/Pt) rows using data_type_colors, keyed by that field's own Data Type. Colour the CIDOC CRM Semantic Node Class and CIDOC CRM Node Class rows using cidoc_class_row_colors (fixed per row, not Data-Type-dependent). The Data Type and Collection rows themselves, and every row below Collection, are not colour-coded - confirmed 2026-09-15 against the real reference workbook (see data_type_colors comment), correcting an earlier, less precise version of this rule.
collection_notation_rules: In the Collection row, if the relationship is to a controlled vocabulary (Concept-list data type), write it as "Name of Vocab (cv)", e.g. "Resource Type (cv)".
In the Collection row, if the relationship is to a resource model (Resource-Instance-List data type), write it as "Name of Model (rm)", e.g. "Actor (rm)".
If the data type is neither Concept-list nor Resource-Instance-List, the Collection cell is not applicable — write "N/A" rather than leaving it blank.
operational_info_rules: If Data type is Resource-Instance-List, operational information is usually "Foreign Key" — unless the value is actually derived from the linked resource, in which case it is "Derived". Not an absolute rule; check the field's meaning.
If Metadata name is MAEASaM ID, operational information is "Primary Key".

If Metadata name is one of "Resource created at", "Resource last modified at" (or "Resource creation at" / "Resource modified at"), "Uploader name", "Upload date", or "Nodes modified", operational information is "Auto-Populated".

dublin_core_terms_in_use._note: Canonical form is the full http://purl.org/dc/terms/<name> URI - not the short dcterms:<name> prefix, and not a dublincore.org spec-page URL (both formats existed in Map/Chronology until 2026-09-07 and were normalized to this form). Full DCMI Metadata Terms vocabulary (all 137 terms, not just these currently-used ones) is in Reference Documents/dublin_core_terms_full.json - check there before assigning an unused term to a field currently marked 'No direct equivalent'. When a field genuinely has no Dublin Core mapping, the Dublin Core Equivalent cell reads 'No direct equivalent' - not 'N/A' (standardized 2026-09-07; 'N/A' remains correct in other columns like Collection/Operational Info, just not this one).

data_type_colors._comment: Cell fill colour (hex RGB, no leading #) used to colour-code a field's Metadata (En/Fr/Ar/Pt) rows in the Excel export/round-trip, keyed by that field's own Data Type. Sourced 2026-09-15 directly from the real hand-coloured reference workbook 20260317_RSMetadata_Template_v02_CURRENT.xlsx (read with openpyxl, not guessed) - confirmed by cross-checking each field's fill colour against its own Data Type row value. 'Semantic' colours the Group row itself (every field's group/card node is Arches datatype 'semantic', so that row is always this one colour regardless of the field's own Data Type). EDTF has no precedent in that file (it split off 'Date' later, 2026-09-09 - see known_issues) so it reuses Date's colour, same family. Boolean has no precedent either - 2026-09-15 pick, not from the reference file. URL, Node, and File-list are genuinely undefined - null, not guessed; fill in only once a real precedent or an explicit decision exists.

cidoc_class_row_colors._comment: Fixed fill colour (hex RGB) for these two CIDOC CRM ontology-class rows, applied uniformly across every field column regardless of that field's Data Type - these describe CIDOC CRM class assignment, not Arches Data Type, so they are a separate concept from data_type_colors above. Same source and date as data_type_colors.

definition_writing_rules: Definitions describe what the value is, as a noun phrase or sentence starting with "The ...", "A ..." or "Whether ..." - not "Records the ...", "This node records ...", "It records ..." or a question ("Who was ...", "What recommendation can you make ..."). End with a full stop. No data-entry instructions ("Please write/enter ...", "This is a required field") - those belong in Input Instructions and Necessity. Adopted 2026-09-25 (Site review; already the style of Actor, Info, Map, Grid).

Definitions (and translated definitions) use sentence case: capitalize only the first word of each sentence and real proper nouns or acronyms (MAEASaM, Arches, WGS 84, CIDOC CRM). Do not capitalize common nouns mid-sentence (write "the type of actor", "a museum", "a hierarchical thesaurus", not "the Type of Actor", "a Museum", "a hierarchical Thesaurus"). Adopted 2026-09-25.

Exception: when a definition lists controlled-vocabulary terms as examples of allowed values, write them exactly as the term appears in the vocabulary (e.g. "e.g. Primary name, Alternative name, Local name"). The same words used in ordinary running prose are lowercase ("a person may have a primary name and an alternative name").
naming_rules: Field names (Metadata (En)) and group names use sentence case: capitalize only the first word plus acronyms and proper nouns (ID, DOI, ISBN, ISSN, URL, EPSG, WKT, APA, MAEASaM). E.g. "Map name", "Digital file name", "Map details" - not "Map Name". Decided 2026-09-25 for all models; applied to Map the same day. The shared Copyright/Access block names (Copyright/Access, Rights Notes, Preferred Citation) and remaining Title Case names in other models are renamed across all templates together, not model by model.
translation_rules: Portuguese translations use European/African Portuguese spelling (pt-PT: registo, ficheiro, contacto, equipa, grelha), matching Mozambique and Guinea-Bissau. Decided 2026-09-25; Map's earlier Brazilian Portuguese (registro, arquivo, grade) was converted the same day.
Translations are made from the current English definition. When the English changes, the French, Arabic and Portuguese texts of that cell must be updated too.

known_issues.title: Arches EDTF datatype silently drops the combined uncertain+approximate qualifier (%)
known_issues.affects: Any node with Arches datatype 'edtf' (project Data Type 'EDTF' as of 2026-09-09 - previously filed under 'Date' before the two were split, see data_type_values)
known_issues.description: Reproduced in Arches 8.1.4 (local test instance): entering a value with the EDTF Level 1 combined uncertain+approximate qualifier, e.g. '2004-06-11%', and saving the tile silently strips the '%' on save - the stored/displayed value becomes '2004-06-11' with no error or warning. Root cause: Arches' EDTFDataType.transform_value_for_tile() (arches/app/datatypes/datatypes.py) re-serializes the input through the third-party 'edtf' Python library (ExtendedDateFormat in arches/app/utils/date_utils.py) via str(parsed_edtf), and that library's string serialization does not round-trip the combined '%' qualifier.
known_issues.confirmed_working: The single qualifiers '?' (uncertain) and '~' (approximate) round-trip correctly on their own, e.g. '1984?' and '2004-06~' are saved and displayed unchanged. Only the combined '%' form is affected.
known_issues.workaround: Avoid the combined '%' qualifier. If a value is both uncertain and approximate, prefer expressing it with '?' or '~' alone, or note the ambiguity in a free-text field, until this is fixed upstream.
known_issues.upstream_issue: Not filed - project decided (2026-09-08) to work around it internally rather than report it upstream for now. The workaround (avoid combined '%') is folded into the 'Date' input_instructions entry above.
known_issues.project_decision: 2026-09-08: proceeding with EDTF adoption for Date-type fields despite this issue - the '?' and '~' qualifiers alone cover most real uncertainty/approximation cases. Combined '%' is flagged as unsupported for now in the Input Instructions.

known_issues.title: Arches URL datatype crashes on bulk-import of blank cells
known_issues.affects: Any node with Arches datatype 'url' (project Data Type 'URL'), when bulk-loaded from Excel/CSV via Arches' business-data importer, if the source column has empty cells for some rows.
known_issues.description: URLDataType.transform_value_for_tile() (arches/app/datatypes/url.py) wraps a plain string in {"url": value, "url_label": ""}, but the bulk-load pipeline reads blank spreadsheet cells as pandas NaN (a float), not an empty string or None. json.loads(nan) and ast.literal_eval(nan) both raise, so transform_value_for_tile falls through to its except BaseException branch and returns {"url": nan, "url_label": ""}. In validate(), value.get("url") is the NaN float, which is truthy in Python, so URLDataType tries self.URL_REGEX.match(nan) - re.match() requires a string, so this raises an uncaught TypeError (not the FailRegexURLMatch the method actually catches), crashing the import instead of producing a normal validation error.
known_issues.confirmed_working: Not independently reproduced against a live traceback this session - diagnosed by reading arches/app/datatypes/url.py against the reported symptom (import failing specifically on blank cells in a URL column). Rows with an actual URL string import fine.
known_issues.workaround: For fields sourced from data where many rows legitimately have no URL (e.g. a Zotero export), use Data Type 'String' instead of 'URL'. The CIDOC ontologyclass/edge stays valid either way (Arches datatype and CIDOC ontologyclass are independent) - only the storage/widget type and the loss of the URL_REGEX format check and the separate url_label sub-field change.
known_issues.upstream_issue: Not filed - same approach as the EDTF issue above, worked around at the project level.
known_issues.project_decision: 2026-09-10: Info's 'URL' field (Zotero import, DOI/Url present for most records but not all) switched from Data Type 'URL' to 'String'. Chronology's 'Digital provenance' field still uses Data Type 'URL' and was not changed - revisit if it is ever bulk-loaded from a source with blank values for that field.
